AIToolbox design system

ArchiMate notation

How AI Toolbox draws its architecture: the ArchiMate figures for the model, and the diagram kinds the model needs beyond ArchiMate (business workflows, process changes, life cycles and detailed design), each generated from a YAML view as PlantUML or Mermaid with one theme.

Notation 2.0 · tokens 5.0.1 · PlantUML 1.2026.8 · Mermaid 11.16 · 62 element types, 21 in the model · 11 relationships · 8 diagram kinds · 24 components: 16 new, 3 changed, 5 kept · 5 taken out

Diagram kindsComponentsElementsRelationshipsRenderers and themes

Diagram kinds

Every diagram is a YAML view in views/: it names the elements, the kind and the renderer, and the generator emits the source with the AIToolbox theme. ArchiMate covers the model; four kinds go beyond it for processes and life cycles, and four for detailed design. Each kind has a default renderer, the one that draws its notation completely; the other is supported.

ArchiMate view

Which elements, across the layers, take part in this, and how are they related?

Phases A to C: motivation, capability maps, process and application cooperation, traceability.

Rules

  • The type decides colour, glyph and shape: the layer colour fills the figure, the glyph is the type.
  • Layers top to bottom: motivation, strategy, business, application. Realization and serving point up.
  • One relationship type per line, named on the line when it carries meaning (drafts the update, writes).
  • An agent is an application component with agent: true: application colours and the line ✦ agent, never teal.
  • Mermaid cannot draw ArchiMate markers: its lines name the type (realization, serving). Use PlantUML for review.

Business workflow

Who does which step, in which order, and where does a person approve what an agent did?

Phase B: the processes of the platform with their agent steps and their review gates (PRI-01).

Rules

  • One lane per role or component; the lane title is its name from the model.
  • The performer decides the look: person (plain), agent (teal, ✦ agent), system (grey, system), review gate (violet, 2 px).
  • Every agent output reaches a review gate before it takes effect; a workflow without one fails review.
  • Decisions are diamonds with a question; their branches are labelled with the answer.
  • The flow starts and ends with a business event. Data objects are notes on the step that reads them.
  • Mermaid has no swimlanes: it writes the lane in the step (Jenkins · system). Use PlantUML when lanes matter.

Process change

What does the target change in this process, compared with what runs today?

Phase B and every change request on a process: the diff reviewed with the pull request.

Rules

  • One diagram: the target, with the removed steps drawn where they were.
  • Marks are computed from the two versions (baseline at a commit, target on a branch), never typed by hand.
  • Added +, changed Δ, moved ↕, removed − (dashed and struck through). Unchanged steps carry no mark.
  • Every mark has its glyph in the label: the colour is never the only cue.
  • A legend says the marks and that unmarked steps are unchanged.

State machine

Which states can this object be in, and what moves it from one to the next?

Phase C data: the life cycle of business and data objects (agent output, model element, change).

Rules

  • States are the object's own statuses, written as in the YAML (In review, not IN_REVIEW).
  • A transition reads event [guard] / action; ✦ marks a transition an agent makes.
  • The current state of an instance is violet with a 2 px border, only when the view shows one instance.
  • One initial state; final states end at the bullseye.

Domain model

Which entities, value objects and aggregates does this module hold, and how do they relate?

Detailed design: refines data objects (DOB-…) into the model a module implements.

Rules

  • Entities in application colours; aggregate roots with a 2 px border; value objects and enumerations in grey.
  • The stereotype is written in words: «aggregate root», «entity», «value object», «enumeration».
  • Multiplicities on both ends of an association; composition when the part does not live without the whole.
  • Written with the code, in the module's detailed design: it refines the model, it is not generated from it.

Interaction

Which messages go between people, agents and components, in which order, for this scenario?

Detailed design: one scenario of a process step, an API call or an agent run.

Rules

  • Participants left to right in the order they first act: person, chat, agent, components, external systems.
  • A person is an actor; an agent is ✦ and teal; components in application colours; external systems grey.
  • Calls are solid with a filled head, returns dashed. Alternatives in alt boxes with the condition in brackets.
  • A review by a person appears as a message from that person, never as a note.

Components and interfaces

Which components make up this application, and which interfaces do they offer and use?

Phase C application and detailed design: application components, interfaces (API-…), external systems.

Rules

  • Components in application colours, external systems grey; an agent component carries ✦ agent.
  • Interfaces are lollipops on the component that offers them; users point at them with a dashed uses.
  • Name interfaces as in the model (Agent API = API-02).
  • Mermaid has no lollipop: interfaces are circles joined to their component.

Data model

Which tables hold this data, with which keys, and how are they joined?

Phase C data and detailed design: the PostgreSQL schema behind the data objects.

Rules

  • Tables in application colours, named as in the database (snake_case).
  • Primary and foreign keys marked PK and FK; mandatory columns starred in PlantUML.
  • Crow's-foot cardinality on both ends; the join named when it is not obvious.

Components

The amended list: 24 components: 16 new, 3 changed, 5 kept · 5 taken out. Colours follow one rule. In ArchiMate, component and table views the layer decides the colour; in workflows and sequences the performer decides it (person, agent, system, review gate). Teal always comes with ✦ agent, and status is never told by colour alone.

ArchiMate notation draw the model · 6

ArchiMate figure

=Kept

One architecture element in its ArchiMate figure: layer fill, 1 px layer ink, type glyph, name.

Change the architecture model
Architecture agent✦ agent
Architecture model
Reviewed knowledge in one repository
Anatomy
  • Layer fill, 1 px layer-ink border, shape from the aspect
  • Glyph 18 px in layer ink: top right in pages, above the name in PlantUML, absent in Mermaid
  • Name: Open Sans 600, 13 / 16, centred, two lines max

Diagram frame how every diagram is shown · 2

Diagram frame

+New

How any generated diagram is shown in the product and in the chat: one frame for every kind and both renderers.

In use: ArchiMate view

Anatomy
  • Header: kind tile, title, view ID, renderer switch (PlantUML · Mermaid) when both exist
  • Body: the SVG on surface-container-lowest, 16 px padding; Fit width or Actual size
  • Footer: model version (@ commit), legend, Source (code block with Copy), Text alternative
Rules
  • Never a screenshot: the SVG is generated from the view at the shown commit.
  • Fit width by default; Actual size scrolls inside the frame, never the page.
  • Dark theme renders with the dark theme of the renderer, not with a CSS filter.

States Loading (skeleton) · Rendered · Error (the renderer's message and the source line, error container) · Stale (the model moved on: Regenerate)

Accessibility The SVG has role=img and the title as its name; the Text alternative button opens the element and relationship list.

Renderers and themes

Both themes are generated from the design-system tokens (5.0.1), in light and dark. The generator writes the include line or appends the class definitions; nobody styles a diagram by hand.

PlantUML

theme/aitoolbox.puml: one include with the colours of both themes, the 59 element procedures with the design-system glyphs, the relationship, step, gate and event procedures, and the styles of the activity, state, class, sequence, component and entity diagrams.

  • Layout by Smetana, built into PlantUML: no Graphviz to install in Jenkins.
  • Checked with PlantUML 1.2026.8 (jar) and the in-browser engine @plantuml/core, which renders every sample under a strict content security policy. The chat and the web pages can render without a server.
  • Dark: !$AX_THEME = "dark" before the include.
@startuml
!$AX_THEME = "dark"          ' optional, light by default
!include aitoolbox.puml
hide stereotype
AX_Goal(GOL01, "Productivity and developer experience")
AX_BusinessProcess(PRC04, "Change the architecture model")
AX_Agent(APC07, "Architecture agent")
AX_RelServing(APC07, PRC04, "drafts the update", "up")
@enduml

Mermaid

theme/aitoolbox-mermaid.json: for each theme, the base theme variables and the class definitions of the layers, performers, change marks, current state and domain-model stereotypes.

  • Checked with Mermaid 11.16 (mermaid-cli).
  • Rendered natively by GitHub, the bank's Git hosting previews and Markdown in the chat: the default for life cycles, classes, sequences and tables.
  • Limits: no ArchiMate markers, no swimlanes, no interface lollipops. Those kinds default to PlantUML.
// mermaid@11
import theme from "./aitoolbox-mermaid.json";
const mode = dark ? "dark" : "light";
mermaid.initialize({ startOnLoad: false, ...theme[mode].config });
const src = view + "\n" + theme[mode].classDefs.join("\n");
const { svg } = await mermaid.render(id, src);
